display.name: Backup
display.description: Whether the nightly backup ran, what it holds, and what Backblaze is storing.

display.name: Backup size
display.description: The dump is what pg_restore would read back; stored is what restic keeps after dedup, and what Backblaze bills for. A dump that falls off a cliff is a backup that succeeded and saved nothing.

spec.query:
SELECT time_bucket($resolution, recorded_timestamp) AS time,
       CASE metric_name WHEN 'backup.snapshot.size' THEN 'dump'
                        ELSE 'stored in b2' END AS series,
       MAX(metric_avg(value)) AS bytes
FROM metrics
WHERE metric_name IN ('backup.snapshot.size', 'backup.repository.size')
  AND recorded_timestamp < time_bucket($resolution, now())
GROUP BY time, series
ORDER BY time DESC;

display.name: Snapshots kept
display.description: Retention is 7 daily, 4 weekly, 12 monthly, so this settles rather than climbs.

spec.query:
SELECT time_bucket($resolution, recorded_timestamp) AS time,
       'snapshots' AS series,
       MAX(metric_avg(value)) AS snapshots
FROM metrics
WHERE metric_name = 'backup.snapshots'
  AND recorded_timestamp < time_bucket($resolution, now())
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time DESC;

display.name: Backup runs
display.description: Both units: the nightly backup and the restore that proves it works.

spec.query:
SELECT start_timestamp,
       attributes->>'systemd.unit' AS unit,
       attributes->>'systemd.result' AS result,
       attributes->>'duration_ms' AS duration_ms
FROM records
WHERE service_name = 'old-news-host'
  AND attributes->>'systemd.unit' LIKE 'old-news-backup%'
ORDER BY start_timestamp DESC
LIMIT 50;
